chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Coming in late on the happy dust scene with Bess
summary: He listens to the music to find his place, talks his way to his song and offers Bess the happy dust, which she refuses.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And I got down on the stage, you could hear a pin fall, only the music you could hear going. Nobody down there saying you go in here, you go in there, here's where you go in. It wasn't that, I had to go in what I heard going on. So I heard the music and I could tell by the sound of the music where I was.

By this time where the police had taken Porgy off the stage to make him look on Crown's face that he just killed -- Crown, Bess wanted to go with him, but she couldn't go no farther than the gate. When she got outside the gate where the wagon was to take Porgy, she turns around to come back and finds me sitting on a keg, that's where she was supposed to find me. They don't pass that part. She done gone out the gate and come back in and started talking to me in the song and the song

she's singing the song to me -- "Sportin' Life they're going to make you look on Crown's face. . ." I'm not there. So I hit the stage, I hear the trill in the music, so that means I'm past that part. I go out on the stage and I start singing -- I start talking -- instead of singing I start talking to catch up, 'cause I couldn't sing to catch up because I'm singing all out of key and out of tune, too. So I just start talking up to the part where she'd be according to the music, and I say, "They're going to lock him up in jail, maybe one year, maybe two years -- "Maybe just like to told you, ain't nobody home now but Bess and ole Sportin' Life. . ." That's when I start singing, and she says, I go to (feed her this happy dust to us to make her go to New York with me, take her away from Porgy. And she says, "Take that stuff away," I don't give up happy dust. And I tell her, "Take that stuff away from you, tell that to somebody else Nobody ever gave up happy dust. . ."

And the music is playing and she don't want the stuff so she stomps at me and she's going to smack this out of my hand, but she didn't. So I kiss it and put it on the step. Like I find out she won't take the happy dust and I want to sing this song to her -- it was just the opposite, just the opposite.

However, while I talk to her up to singing that song, to where I sing it '' goin' to lock him up in jail -- "Maybe one year, maybe two years, Just like I told you, ain't nobody home now But Bess and ole Sportin' Life . . ." When I got to there, "Come on, Bess, try it." "Give up that happy dust," "Give it up, huh? Tell that to somebody else, nobody ever gave up happy dust."

And then Porgy comes out to run me away and he falls down on the stage, he fell on his hand and I laid down so he could get my arm and show that he got me and he wrestled me, I got away and I says, "All right, don't want another shot, eh?"
